newsitem.title: INDIA: ITC drives Delhi shares to sharply higher close.
newsitem.headline: ITC drives Delhi shares to sharply higher close.

text.p: Cigarette and hotel conglomerate ITC led the charge as share prices ended sharply higher ahead of the settlement on the Delhi Stock Exchange on Thursday, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 17.40 points higher at 905.43.

"ITC was in the spotlight on heavy short-covering by speculators and large scale buying by foreign investors, fuelled by reports of strong first quarter results by the company," S.C. Juneja of stockbrokers Jaico Credit said.
The Business Standard newspaper said ITC had reported a 34 percent jump in net profit for the first quarter of 1997/98 (April-March) ending June 30, 1997.
ITC rose 43.80 rupees, or 9.3 percent, to 517.50.
Reliance Industries ended 5.40 rupees higher at 357.55.
State Bank of India firmed 7.75 rupees to 324.10.
Automaker TELCO dropped 0.20 rupee to 389.30 on scattered selling following the announcement of lower-than-expected first quarter results by the company, brokers said.
TELCO on Wednesday reported sales of 18.80 billion rupees in the first quarter of 1997/98 (April-March), a 10 percent drop from the same period last year.
